claims.explanation: Tyrphostin AG-99 is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and the most sensitive lines are enriched for EGFR-pathway activation, particularly EGFR mutation/amplification (HCC4006) and RAS/MAPK pathway mutations (KRAS, BRAF, HRAS, NF1) that can create dependence on EGFR signaling. Conversely, many resistant lines lack EGFR-pathway alterations or have mutations in downstream effectors such as PIK3CA/PTEN that bypass EGFR inhibition. The pattern suggests selectivity is driven by EGFR dependency, with additional contribution from loss of tumor suppressors like NF2 or STK11 that may modulate sensitivity.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant HCC4006 is among the most killed lines; EGFR is the annotated target
KRAS-mutant lines (PATU8988S, RKN, SNU81) are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via EGFR-dependent MAPK signaling
BRAF-mutant lines (22RV1, NMCG1, SNUC5) appear in the sensitive set
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and may increase EGFR dependence; seen in sensitive lines (COLO792, PLCPRF5, KALS1, SNU81)
HRAS-mutant T24 is sensitive, consistent with MAPK pathway activation
PTEN mutations are more common in resistant lines (ESS1, SNU466, RL952, HEC265, DMS273), suggesting PI3K/AKT bypass
PIK3CA mutations appear in several resistant lines (HGC27, ESS1, RL952, HEC265) and may reduce EGFR dependence
NF2-mutant lines (NMCG1, NCIH2052, SNU410) are split but NF2 loss may sensitize to EGFR inhibition in mesothelioma
STK11 mutations appear in sensitive lines (TE4, 22RV1, PLCPRF5, KALS1) but also some resistant, weak evidence
TP53 mutations are ubiquitous and not selective; included only as a weak trend
ARID1A mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, not selective
ATM mutations are enriched in resistant lines (TE9, RL952, SNU685, ESS1), possibly via DNA damage response
